My First Train Trip Alone: 第一次独自坐火车去两百公里外的阿姨家:找站台、靠窗看风景、邻座帮忙放行李箱。

Last summer, I took a train alone for the first time, from my city to my aunt's home two hundred kilometres away. My parents drove me to the station, and my hands were a little shaky when they said goodbye.

Finding the right platform was not easy for me. I asked a worker in a blue uniform, and she showed me the way with a smile. On the train, I sat by the window and watched fields, rivers and small towns pass by like a slow film.

A kind man next to me helped me put my suitcase on the shelf. An hour and a half later, I saw my aunt waiting at the exit. The trip taught me that travelling alone is not so scary — it is the beginning of growing up.
